en: Pertaining to ideas, or to a given idea.
Existing only in the mind; conceptual, imaginary.
A perfect standard of beauty, intellect etc., or a standard of excellence to aim at.
A two-sided ideal; a subset of a ring which is closed under both left and right multiplication by elements of the ring.

ideal.ety:
From French idéal, from Late Latin ideālis (“existing in idea”), by surface analysis, idea + -al, from Latin idea (“idea”); see idea.
In mathematics, the noun ring theory sense was first introduced by German mathematician Richard Dedekind in his 1871 edition of a text on number theory. The concept was quickly expanded to ring theory and later generalised to order theory. The set theory and Lie theory senses can be regarded as applications of the order theory sense.

ex.en: The house isn't ideal, but it's all right.
ex.ja: その家は理想的とはいえないが、まぁさしつかえはない。

ex.en: I know an ideal place for a party.
ex.ja: パーティーのためのうってつけの場所を知ってるよ。

ex.en: The new method was anything but ideal.
ex.ja: その新しい方法は理想からほど遠かった。

note.ja: ラテン語 idealis から。ギリシャ語 idea（形・姿）。「頭の中の完全な姿」→「理想（的な）」。idea と同じ。

Emotional character (of a work of music, literature, or other art).

settle.ety:
From a merger of two verbs:
* Middle English setlen, from Old English setlan (“to settle, seat, put to rest”), from Old English setl (“seat”) (compare Dutch zetelen (“to be established, settle”)) and
* Middle English sahtlen, seihtlen (“to reconcile, calm, subside”), from Old English sahtlian, ġesehtlian (“to reconcile”), from Old English saht, seht (“settlement, agreement, reconciliation, peace”) (see saught, -le).
German siedeln (“to settle”) is related to the former of the two verbs, but is not an immediate cognate of either of them.

en: The act of sending a legislative bill to committee for review.
Official consignment sending a person to prison or a mental health institution.

ex.en: I've got another commitment this evening.
ex.ja: 今日の夕方には、別の約束があるのです。

ex.ja: 私たちはすでに家族ぐるみのお付き合いがあります。

ex.en: You've got to carry out your commitment at all costs.
ex.ja: 自分が堅く誓ったことは、どんなことがあっても実行しなければいけないよ。

en: Very sure of something; positive.
Self-assured, self-reliant, sure of oneself.

confident.ety: From Middle French confident, from Latin confidens (“confident, i.e. self-confident, in a good or bad sense, bold, daring, audacious, impudent”), present participle of confidere (“to trust fully, confide”). See confide.

ex.en: I am confident he will keep his promise.
ex.ja: 私は彼が約束を守ることを確信している。

ex.en: I'm confident that I'll win the tennis match.
ex.ja: 僕はこのテニスの試合に勝てるという確信がある。

ex.en: I'm confident that there won't be a world war.
ex.ja: もはや世界大戦はないものと確信する。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ fid（信頼する）+ ent。完全に信じている →「自信のある・確信して」。

en: Frequent repetition of the same behavior; way of behavior common to many; ordinary manner; habitual practice; method of doing, living or …
Habitual buying of goods from one same vendor.
Made or done in a way adjusted to fit the needs of a particular person or group (e.g., customer, health care patient, do-it-yourselfer), …
Own, personal, not standard or premade.

From Middle English custume, borrowed from Anglo-Norman custume, inherited from Latin consuētūdinem, a noun derived from cōnsuēscō, from con- (“with”) + suēscō (“become used or accustomed to”). Displaced native Old English ġewuna and sidu. Doublet of costume, consuetude, and kastom.

ex.en: Is it a general custom in your country?

ex.ja: その習慣はずっと以前にすたれてしまった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 costume（習慣）から。ラテン語 consuetudo。「習慣」→（customs）慣習的に取る「関税・税関」。customer、costume と同じ。

en: To disallow or reject.
To assert that something is not true.

deny.ety: From Middle English denyen, from Old French denoier (“to deny, to repudiate”) (French dénier), from Latin denegare (“to deny, to refuse”), from de- (“away”) and negare (“to refuse”), the latter ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *né (“no, not”). Doublet of denegate.

ex.en: It cannot be denied that he is guilty.
ex.ja: 彼が有罪であることは否定できない。

ex.en: He denied having taken part in the crime.
ex.ja: 彼はその犯罪に加わったことを否定した。

ex.en: She denied having taken part in the scheme.
ex.ja: 彼女はそのたくらみに加わったことを否定した。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ ny（否定する）。ラテン語 denegare から。完全に否定する →「否定する・拒む」。negative と同じ neg。

en: A table, frame, or case, in past centuries usually with a sloping top but now usually with a flat top, for the use of writers and readers…
A reading table or lectern to support the book from which the liturgical service is read, differing from the pulpit from which the sermon…
To shut up, as in a desk; to treasure.
To equip with a desk or desks.

desk.ety: From Middle English deske, desque, from Medieval Latin desca, modified from Old Italian desco, from Latin discus. Doublet of dais, disc, discus, dish, disk, and diskos. See also German Tisch, "table".

ex.en: The money on the desk is not mine.
ex.ja: 机の上のお金は私のものではありません。

ex.en: There is only one book on the desk.
ex.ja: 机の上には本が１冊しかない。

ex.en: There are not any books under the desk.
ex.ja: 机の下には本はありません。

note.ja: ラテン語 discus（円盤・皿）からイタリア語 desco（机）を経た語。disk、dish と同じ語源。

en: The organ of hearing, consisting of the pinna or auricle, auditory canal, eardrum, malleus, incus, stapes and cochlea.
The external part of the organ of hearing, the auricle.
To take in with the ears; to hear.
To hold by the ears.

ex.ja: あなたの話をして下さい。熱心に聞きますから。

ex.en: I hear a noise offensive to the ear.
ex.ja: 耳障りな音が聞こえる。

en: A person who works the land and/or who keeps livestock; anyone engaged in agriculture on a farm.
More specifically, a farm owner, as distinguished from a farmworker or farmhand as a hired employee thereof.

farmer.ety: From Middle English fermour (“a steward, bailliff, collector of taxes”), from Old French fermier (“a farmer, a lessee, husbandman, bailliff”), from Medieval Latin firmarius (“one to whom land is rented, a collector of taxes, deputy”), from firma; equivalent to farm + -er. Compare Old English feormere (“a purveyor of a guild, a supplier of food, a grocer, farmer”). More at farm.

ex.en: The farmers must be happy to hear that.
ex.ja: お百姓さんはそれを聞いて喜ぶに違いない。

ex.en: There were once poor farmers in that village.
ex.ja: かつて、その村に、貧しい農夫がいた。

ex.en: Some farmers are working on the farm.
ex.ja: 農場にはいく人かの人々が働いています。

note.ja: farm（農場）+ -er。「農場経営者」。

en: A sports facility specialized for lifting weights, cardio machines, and other exercise (culturally differentiated from sense 1).
Physical education class (PE class).
To go to the gym.

ex.en: I don't like changing into my gym clothes.
ex.ja: 体操服に着替えるのやだな。

ex.en: This hotel has a gym and a swimming pool.
ex.ja: このホテルには体育館とプールが備わっている。

ex.en: There are a lot of students in the gym.
ex.ja: 体育館にたくさんの生徒がいます。

note.ja: gymnasium の短縮。ギリシャ語 gymnos（裸の）。

en: Furnishing help; gives aid; useful.

helpful.ety: From Middle English helpful; equivalent to help + -ful.

ex.en: Tony gave us a piece of helpful advice.
ex.ja: トニーは私たちに役に立つ助言を１つした。

ex.en: This book will be helpful to your study.
ex.ja: この本は君の勉強に役立つだろう。

ex.en: Your comments were always very helpful to me.
ex.ja: あなたの批評はいつも私には有益でした。

note.ja: help（助け）+ -ful。「役に立つ」。

en: An intense distressing emotion of fear or repugnance.
Something horrible; that which excites horror.

horror.ety: From Middle English horer, horrour, from Old French horror, from Latin horror (“a bristling, a shaking, trembling as with cold or fear, terror”), from horrere (“to bristle, shake, be terrified”). Displaced native Old English ōga.

ex.en: She drew back in horror at the sight.
ex.ja: 彼女はその光景を見て恐怖で後ずさりした。

ex.en: She threw her arms around him in horror.
ex.ja: 彼女は恐ろしさのあまり彼に抱きついた。

ex.en: I like all kinds of movies except horror.
ex.ja: 映画はホラー以外なら何でも好きです。

note.ja: ラテン語 horror（身の毛がよだつこと）から。horrere（毛が逆立つ）。horrible、horrify と同じ。

en: A small ticket or sign giving information about something to which it is attached or intended to be attached.
A name given to something or someone to categorise them as part of a particular social group.
To put a label (a ticket or sign) on (something).
To give (a label) to (someone or something) in order to categorise that person or thing.

label.ety: From Middle English label (“narrow band, strip of cloth”), from Old French label, lambel (Modern French lambeau), from Frankish *lappā (“torn piece of cloth”), from Proto-Germanic *lappǭ, *lappô (“cloth stuff, rag, scraps, flap, dewlap, lobe, rabbit ear”), from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“blade”). Cognate with Old High German lappa (“rag, piece of cloth”), Old English læppa (“skirt, flap of a garment”). More at lap.

ex.en: He attached a label to the bag.
ex.ja: 彼は鞄にラベルを貼った。

ex.en: He attached a "Fragile" label to the package.
ex.ja: 彼は「壊れ物注意」のステッカーを荷物に貼り付けた。

ex.en: The label is attached to the trunk.
ex.ja: 荷札がトランクについている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 label（細長い布切れ）から。「札」→「ラベル」→ レコード会社の「レーベル」。

en: Bare, not covered by clothing.
Unadorned, without decoration or circumlocution; put bluntly.

naked.ety: From Middle English naked, from Old English nacod, from Proto-West Germanic *nak(k)wad, from Proto-Germanic *nakwadaz, from Proto-Indo-European *negʷ- (“naked”). Doublet of nude (remotely).

ex.en: What's wrong with running around your house naked?
ex.ja: 自分の家を裸で練り歩いて何が悪い！

ex.en: When Mary saw Tom naked, she started laughing.
ex.ja: トムが裸でいるのを見て、メアリーは笑い出した。

ex.en: It isn't really visible to the naked eye.
ex.ja: それは裸眼にはそこまではっきり見ることはできない。

note.ja: 古英語 nacod から。ラテン語 nudus（nude）と同じ祖先。「裸の」。

en: Production; quantity produced, created, or completed.
Data sent out of the computer, as to output device such as a monitor or printer, or data sent from one program on the computer to another.
To produce, create, or complete.
To send data out of a computer, as to an output device such as a monitor or printer, or to send data from one program on the computer to …

output.ety: From out + (verb) put; nominalisation of put out.

ex.ja: この工場の生産高は２０％増加している。

ex.en: The output is way below last year's level.
ex.ja: 生産高は昨年の水準よりはるかに落ちこんでいる。

ex.en: Last year's output of coal fell short of the standard.
ex.ja: 昨年の石炭生産高は水準に達しなかった。

note.ja: out（外へ）+ put（出す）。「生産高・出力」。input の対。

en: A sticky, gummy substance secreted by trees; tree sap.
Anything similar to or derived from tree sap: resin; rosin.
To cover or smear with pitch.
To darken; to blacken; to obscure.
Very dark black; pitch-black.
Intense, deep, dark.

pitch.ety: From Middle English picche, piche, pich, from Old English piċ, from Proto-West Germanic *pik, from Latin pix. Cognate with Ancient Greek πίσσα (píssa, “pitch, tar”), Latin pīnus (“pine”). More at pine. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Pik (“pitch, tar”), Dutch pek (“pitch, tar”), German Low German Pick (“pitch, tar”), German Pech (“pitch, tar”), Catalan pega (“pitch”), Spanish pegar (“to stick, glue”), Franco-Provençal pouatche (“sap from a pine”) and French poix (“sap”). The adjective is probably back-formed from pitch-black, reinterpreting "pitch" as meaning "intense(ly)".

ex.en: I wish you could have seen him pitch.
ex.ja: 彼の投球を見せたかったよ。

ex.en: How can I sing better at a high pitch?
ex.ja: 高い声ってどうやったらうまく出せるの？

ex.en: Everybody will have to pitch in to save the environment.
ex.ja: 環境を救うために、みんなが拠出も含めた協力をしなければならないでしょう。

note.ja: 中英語 picchen（突き刺す・投げる）から。「投げる」→「投球」→ 音の「高さ」→ 競技場の「ピッチ」。黒い「ピッチ（瀝青）」は別語。

en: A baked Italian dish of a thinly rolled bread crust typically topped before baking with tomato sauce, cheese, and other ingredients such …
A single instance of this dish.

pizza.ety:
First attested in 1931, borrowed from Neapolitan pizza (1590), of uncertain origin. Possibly related to Medieval Greek πίτα (píta, “cake, pie”), attested in 1107 and itself of uncertain origin.
The northern Italian dialectal form was pinza, the southern (Apulian and Calabrian) form was pitta. This suggests a derivation from Latin pīnctus (pictus (“painted, smeared”)) or pīnsum, pīnsitum, pistum (“pounded”), but the northern forms appear to be contaminated with pinzare (“to staple”).

ex.en: The pizza delivery guy hasn't come by yet.
ex.ja: ピザの宅配の人、まだ来ないのよ。

ex.ja: ピザ屋さんの電話番号って、何番？

ex.en: When was the last time you ate pizza?
ex.ja: 最後にピザ食べたのはいつですか？

note.ja: イタリア語 pizza から。語源ははっきりしない。

en: Ordinary; lacking adornment or ornamentation; unembellished.
Of just one colour; lacking a pattern.
Simply.
An expanse of land with relatively low relief and few trees, especially a grassy expanse.
A broad, flat expanse in general, as of water.

plain.ety: From Middle English pleyn, borrowed from Anglo-Norman pleyn, playn, Middle French plain, plein, and Old French plain, from Latin plānus (“flat, even, level, plain”). Doublet of llano, piano, plane, and plan.

ex.en: It is plain that you are to blame.
ex.ja: 君が悪いことははっきりしている。

ex.en: That she was tired was plain to see.
ex.ja: 彼女が疲れているのは見て明らかだった。

ex.en: To do her justice, she is not plain.
ex.ja: 彼女を公平に評価すれば、彼女は不器量ではない。

note.ja: ラテン語 planus（平らな）から。「平らな」→「明白な・質素な」→「平原」。plane、explain と同じ。

en: To bring up to maturity, as offspring; to educate; to instruct; to foster.
To breed and raise.
Being behind, or in the hindmost part; hindmost.
The back or hindmost part; that which is behind, or last in order.
Specifically, the part of an army or fleet which comes last, or is stationed behind the rest.

rear.ety:
From Middle English reren (“to raise”), from Old English rǣran (“to raise, set upright, promote, exalt, begin, create, give rise to, excite, rouse, arouse, stir up”), from Proto-West Germanic *raiʀijan, from Proto-Germanic *raizijaną, *raisijaną (“to cause to rise, raise”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rey- (“to lift oneself, rise”).
Cognate with Scots rere (“to construct, build, rear”), Icelandic reisa (“to raise”), Gothic 𐍂𐌰𐌹𐍃𐌾𐌰𐌽 (raisjan, “to cause to rise, lift up, establish”), German reisen (“to travel”, literally “to rear up and depart”); and a doublet of raise. More at rise.

ex.en: Please move to the rear of the bus.
ex.ja: バスの後方へお詰め願います。

ex.ja: 母は私たちを育てるために一生懸命働いた。

ex.en: Many people pushed their way toward the rear exit.
ex.ja: たくさんの人々が他人を押し分けて後部出口に向かった。

note.ja: 「後ろ」は arrear（遅れ）の短縮で、ラテン語 retro（後ろへ）から。「育てる」は古英語 rǣran（起こす）からで別語（raise と同系）。

en: Of a work of literature, a writer etc.: being like or having the characteristics of a romance, or poetic tale of a mythic or quasi-histor…
Fantastic, unrealistic (of an idea etc.); fanciful, sentimental, impractical (of a person).
A person with romantic character (a character like those of the knights in a mythic romance).
A person who is behaving romantically (in a manner befitting someone who feels an idealized form of love).

ex.ja: ロマンティックなディナーにはもってこいの場所だ。

ex.en: He, if anything, is the romantic type.
ex.ja: どちらかと言えば、彼はロマンチストだ。

ex.en: I like him, but not in a romantic way.
ex.ja: 彼のこと好きだけど、恋愛対象っていうことじゃないのよ。

en: Of or pertaining to strategy.
Of or relating to military operations that are more large-scale or long-range than local or tactical ones.

strategic.ety: From Ancient Greek στρατηγικός (stratēgikós, “of or for a general", also "a treatise on strategy”), from στρατηγός (stratēgós, “the leader or commander of an army, a general”), from στρατός (stratós, “army”) + ἄγω (ágō, “I lead, I conduct”).

ex.ja: その会社はアジアに進出するという戦略的な決定をした。

en: To move through the water, without touching the bottom; to propel oneself in water by natural means.
To become immersed in, or as if in, or flooded with, or as if with, a liquid.
An act or instance of swimming.
The sound, or air bladder, of a fish.

swim.ety:

ex.en: Swimming in the ocean is my greatest pleasure.
ex.ja: 海で泳ぐことは私の一番の楽しみだ。

ex.en: Would you like to go swimming with us?
ex.ja: 一緒に泳ぎに行きませんか。

ex.en: Is Mike a member of the swimming club?
ex.ja: マイクは水泳部の部員ですか。

note.ja: 古英語 swimman から。「泳ぐ」。

en: Health, safety, happiness and prosperity; well-being in any respect.
Shortened form of "welfare spending", "welfare payments", or "welfare assistance".
To provide with welfare or aid.

welfare.ety: From Middle English welefare, probably from the Old English phrase wel faran (“to fare well, get along successfully, prosper”) (cognate with Middle Dutch welvare (“welfare”), Middle Low German wolvare (“welfare”), Middle High German wolvar, wolfar (“welfare”)). ex.en: I think welfare isn't enough to go around.
ex.ja: 福祉は十分に行き渡っていないように思うんですけど。

ex.en: National welfare is the end of politics.
ex.ja: 国民の幸福が政治の目的である。

ex.en: We did everything for the welfare of our children.
ex.ja: 私たちは子供の幸福のためにあらゆることをした。

note.ja: well（よく）+ fare（行く・暮らす）。「よく暮らすこと」→「福祉」。farewell（さようなら：よい旅を）と同じ fare。

en: Metal formed into a thin, even thread, now usually by being drawn through a hole in a steel die.
A piece of such material; a thread or slender rod of metal, a cable.
To fasten with wire, especially with reference to wine bottles, corks, or fencing.
To string on a wire.

wire.ety: From Middle English wir, wyr, from Old English wīr (“wire, metal thread, wire-ornament”), from Proto-Germanic *wīraz (“wire”), from Proto-Indo-European *weh₁iros (“a twist, thread, cord, wire”), from *weh₁y- (“to turn, twist, weave, plait”).

ex.en: Send a wire to your father right now.
ex.ja: お父さんにすぐ電報を打ちなさい。

ex.en: I will wire you when I get there.
ex.ja: 着いたら電報で知らせるよ。

ex.en: In a town you may pass unnoticed, whereas in a village it's impossible.
ex.ja: 都会では気付かれず通り過ぎることもあるだろうが、村の中ではそうはいかない。

en: To get.
To gain, usually by one's own exertions; to get as one's own.

acquire.ety: From Middle English acqueren, from Old French aquerre, from Latin acquirō; ad- + quaerō (“to seek for”). See quest.

ex.en: That which is easily acquired is easily lost.
ex.ja: 簡単に手に入れたものはすぐに失いやすい。

ex.en: The word has acquired a broad meaning.
ex.ja: その語は広い意味を持つに至った。

ex.en: He acquired the ability to speak English.
ex.ja: 彼は英語を話す能力を身につけた。

note.ja: ac（〜へ）+ quir（求める）。求めて手に入れる →「獲得する・身につける」。

en: The state of being allied.
The act of allying or uniting.

alliance.ety: From Middle English alliaunce, from Old French aliance (French alliance). Equivalent to ally + -ance. Compare with Doric Greek ἁλία (halía, “assembly”). See also al-.

ex.en: Germany made an alliance with Italy.
ex.ja: ドイツはイタリアと同盟を結んだ。

ex.en: Japan entered into an alliance with France just before the war.
ex.ja: 戦争の直前、日本がフランスと同盟を結びました。

ex.en: He argued for our forming the alliance with that nation.
ex.ja: 彼は我が国がその国と同盟を結ぶのに賛成すべきだと論じた。

note.ja: ally（同盟する）+ -ance。ラテン語 alligare ＝ ad + ligare（結ぶ）。「結びつくこと」→「同盟」。league、religion と同じ lig。

en: To issue a command; to tell.
To invite; to summon.
An offer at an auction, or to carry out a piece of work.
A (failed) attempt to receive or intercept a pass.

bid.ety:
From Middle English bidden, from Old English biddan (“to ask, demand”), from Proto-West Germanic *biddjan, from Proto-Germanic *bidjaną (“to ask”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰedʰ-. Conflated with Old English bēodan (“to offer, announce”) (see Etymology 2 below).
Compare West Frisian bidde, Low German bidden, Dutch bidden ("to pray"), German bitten, Danish bede, Norwegian Bokmål be.

ex.en: We should put out a call for bids.
ex.ja: あいみつ取るべきだね。

ex.en: The corporation invited bids for the construction project.
ex.ja: 公団は建設計画の入札を募集した。

ex.en: I bid ten dollars for the old stove.
ex.ja: 私は古いストーブに１０ドルの値をつけた。

note.ja: 古英語 biddan（頼む）と bēodan（申し出る）が混ざった語。「申し出る」→「入札・付け値」→「試み」。

en: A friend or casual acquaintance.
A partner for a particular activity.
A person far removed from the conversation.
To assign a buddy, or partner, to.
Resembling a bud.

buddy.ety: First appears c. 1788, in the writings of Charles Dibdin, of uncertain origin. Possibly from *bruddy, *bruthy, a child-talk alteration of brother. Alternatively, perhaps from British colloquial butty (“companion”), also the form of an older dialect term meaning workmate, associated with coal mining. Itself believed derived from 1530 as booty fellow, a partner with whom one shares booty or loot. Alternatively, compare Scots buddo, bodda (“buddy, kiddo, dear”), related to Icelandic budda (“purse"; also "short, stout person”).

ex.en: A thing you should have is friends, buddy!
ex.ja: 持つべきものは友よ友！

ex.en: Something you ought to have is friends, buddy!
ex.ja: 持つべきものは友よ友！

ex.en: A thing you ought to have is friends, buddy!
ex.ja: 持つべきものは友よ友！

note.ja: brother（兄弟）の幼児語 bud から変化したとされる。「相棒」。

To place in the ground.
A borough; a manor

en: The end, finish, close or last part of something.
The outcome or result of a process or act.

conclusion.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French conclusion, from Latin conclūsiō, from the past participle stem of conclūdere (“to conclude”), from con- + claudō, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂u- (“key, hook, nail”). By surface analysis, conclude + -sion.

ex.en: How did you arrive at such a conclusion?
ex.ja: どうしてそんな結論に到達したのですか。

ex.en: By way of conclusion he said as follows.
ex.ja: 結論として彼は次のように言った。

ex.en: How did you arrive at this conclusion?
ex.ja: どのようにしてこの結論に達したのですか。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ clus（閉じる）+ ion。完全に閉じること →「結論・終わり」。

en: Expressing praise and approval, expressing approbation.

ex.en: He offered his congratulations on the happy occasion.
ex.ja: そのめでたいときに当たり彼は祝辞を述べた。

ex.en: Congratulations on coming first in the competition.
ex.ja: その競技で優勝したそうで、おめでとうございます。

ex.en: He sent me his congratulations by wire.
ex.ja: 彼は私に祝電を打ってよこした。

note.ja: congratulate（祝う）+ -ion の複数形。con（共に）+ gratulari（喜ぶ）。grateful と同じ grat。

en: To make someone believe, or feel sure about something, especially by using logic, argument or evidence.
To persuade.

convince.ety: Borrowed from Latin convincō (“to refute, prove”), from con- + vincō (“to conquer, vanquish”). Doublet of convict. Displaced native Old English oferreċċan.

ex.en: You will soon be convinced I am right.
ex.ja: 君はすぐに私が正しいことを確信するでしょう。

ex.en: I am convinced that my son is innocent.
ex.ja: 私は息子の潔白を信じています。

ex.en: I am convinced that he did nothing wrong.
ex.ja: 私は彼が何も間違いをしていないと確信している。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ vinc（打ち勝つ）。完全に言い負かす →「納得させる・確信させる」。

en: A solid composed of an array of atoms or molecules possessing long-range order and arranged in a pattern which is periodic in three dimen…
A piece of glimmering, shining mineral resembling ice or glass.
Made of crystal.
Very clear; coherent.

crystal.ety: From Middle English crystal, cristal, criȝstall, representing a merger of Old English cristalla (from Latin crystallus) and Anglo-Norman cristall, Old French cristal (from Latin crystallum). The Latin is derived from Ancient Greek κρύσταλλος (krústallos, “clear ice”), from κρύος (krúos, “frost”), from Proto-Indo-European *krews- (“hard, hard outer surface, crust”).

ex.en: There is a big crystal in his room.
ex.ja: 彼の部屋には大きなクリスタルがある。

ex.en: A crystal chandelier was hanging over the table.
ex.ja: ガラス製のシャンデリアがテーブルの真上に下がっていた。

ex.en: Emoto Masaru believes that within ice crystals you can read a message to mankind.
ex.ja: 江本勝は氷の結晶に人類へのメッセージが読みとれると思っています。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 krystallos（氷）から。透明な水晶を氷が固まったものと考えた。

en: Appropriate; suitable for the circumstances.
Having a suitable conformity to basic moral standards; showing integrity, fairness, or other characteristics associated with moral uprigh…

decent.ety: Borrowed from Middle French décent, or its source, Latin decēns, present participle of decet (“it is fitting or suitable”), from Proto-Indo-European *deḱ- (“to take, accept, to receive, greet, be suitable”) (compare Ancient Greek δοκέω (dokéō, “to appear, seem, think”), δέχομαι (dékhomai, “to accept”); Sanskrit दशस्यति (daśasyáti, “shows honor, is gracious”), दाशति (dāśati, “makes offerings, bestows”)). Meaning ‘kind, pleasant’ is from 1902.

ex.en: Why don't you get yourself a decent house?
ex.ja: まともな家に住んだらどう？

ex.en: I'd like to live in a decent house.
ex.ja: まともな家に住みたいよ。

ex.en: It's very decent of you to help me.
ex.ja: お手伝いくださってどうもありがとう。

note.ja: ラテン語 decens（ふさわしい）から。decere（ふさわしい）。「ちゃんとした・かなりの」。decorate と同系。

en: Downward movement, fall.
A sloping downward, e.g. of a hill or road.
To move downwards, to fall, to drop.
To become weaker or worse.

decline.ety:
From Middle English declinen, and ultimately Latin declīnō (“to bend, turn aside, deflect, inflect, decline”, from dē- (“down”) + clīnō (“to bend, to incline”)), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱley- (English lean). The senses arrived from two separate pathways in Middle English:
* The grammatical sense came from Old English declīnian, which was borrowed directly from the Latin etymon.
* All senses except the grammatical sense were derived from those of Old French decliner. Old French itself borrowed the verb from Latin.

ex.en: There was a rapid decline in stock prices.
ex.ja: 株価の急激な下落があった。

ex.en: All of us want prices to decline.
ex.ja: 我々は皆物価が下がるのを望んでいる。

ex.en: The institution of marriage appears to be on the decline.
ex.ja: 結婚という制度はあまり重要ではなくなってきているようだ。

note.ja: de（下へ）+ clin（傾く）。下へ傾く →「衰える・低下（する）・断る」。

en: A period of time before an event occurs; the act of delaying; procrastination; lingering inactivity.
An audio effects unit that introduces a controlled delay.
To put off until a later time; to defer.
To retard; to temporarily stop, detain, or hinder.

delay.ety:
From Middle English delaien, borrowed from Anglo-Norman delaier, Old French deslaier, from des- + Old French laier (“to leave”), a conflation of Old Frankish *lattjan ("to delay, hinder"; from Proto-Germanic *latjaną (“to delay, hinder, stall”), from Proto-Indo-European *leh₁d- (“to leave, leave behind”)), and Old Frankish *laibijan ("to leave"; from Proto-Germanic *laibijaną (“to leave, cause to stay”), from Proto-Indo-European *leyp- (“to remain, continue”)). Doublet of dally.
Akin to Old English latian (“to delay, hesitate”), Old English latu (“a delay, a hindrance”), Old English lǣfan (“to

ex.en: We should deal with this matter without delay.
ex.ja: 我々は直ちにこの問題に対処しなければならない。

ex.en: I'm sorry for the delay in my reply.
ex.ja: お返事が遅れまして、申し訳ありません。

ex.en: I must set about that work without delay.
ex.ja: 私はすぐにその仕事に取りかからねばならない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 delaier から。de + laier（残す）。「後に残す」→「遅らせる」。relay と同じ。

en: A barren area of land or desolate terrain, especially one with little water or vegetation; a wasteland.
In particular, a barren, arid area of land which is hot, with sandy, rocky, or parched ground.
Usually of a place: abandoned, deserted, or uninhabited.
To leave (anything that depends on one's presence to survive, exist, or succeed), especially when contrary to a promise or obligation; to…
To leave one's duty or post, especially to leave a military or naval unit without permission.

desert.ety: From Middle English desert (“wilderness”), from Old French desert, from Latin dēsertum, past participle of dēserō (“to abandon”). Generally displaced native Old English wēsten. False cognate of Egyptian dšrt.

ex.en: This is an animal found in that desert.
ex.ja: これはその砂漠で見つけられた動物だ。

ex.en: They shot the film in an actual desert.
ex.ja: 彼等は実際の砂漠で映画を撮影した。

ex.en: There's a lot of sand in the desert.
ex.ja: 砂漠にはたくさんの砂があります。

note.ja: 「砂漠」はラテン語 desertum（見捨てられた土地）から。「見捨てる」も同じ語（de + serere：つなぐ → つながりを断つ）。「当然の報い（deserts）」は deserve からで別語。

en: Of, relating to, or situated in the central business district.
In or towards the central business district.
Outside the three-point line, or generally far from the basket.
The main business part of a city or town, usually located at or near its center.

ex.en: What platform does the downtown train leave from?
ex.ja: ダウンタウン行きは何番線ですか。

ex.en: Are you sure you want to move downtown?
ex.ja: 本当に都心に引っ越ししたいのか？

ex.en: Let's have lunch downtown and take in a show.
ex.ja: 街でお昼を食べて、映画でも見よう。

note.ja: down（下の方）+ town。マンハッタン南部（地図の下）の中心街から。

en: Of high birth or social position; aristocratic or patrician.
Representing the choicest or most select of a group.
A special group or social class of people who have a superior social or economic status and attendant power, advantages, or privileges in…
An individual member of such a group.

elite.ety: From Middle English elit, from Old French elit, eslit (“chosen, elected”) past participle of elire, eslire (“to choose, elect”), from Latin eligere (“to choose, elect”), with past participle electus; see elect.

ex.en: You are now among the elite.
ex.ja: 君はいまやエリート集団の一員だ。

ex.en: On the whole, the elite are not sensitive to criticism.
ex.ja: 概してエリート達は批判に対して鈍感である。

ex.en: Tom goes to an elite university.
ex.ja: トムは一流大学に行っています。

note.ja: フランス語 élite（選ばれた）から。élire（選ぶ）、ラテン語 eligere。elect と同じ。

ja: 外へ（back and forth：行ったり来たり）

forth.ety: From Middle English forth, from Old English forþ, from Proto-West Germanic *forþ, from Proto-Germanic *furþą, from Proto-Indo-European *pŕ̥-to-, from *per-. Cognates include Dutch voort and German fort. See also ford.

ex.en: I walked back and forth on the street.
ex.ja: 私は通りを行ったり来たりした。

ex.en: He walked back and forth on the street.
ex.ja: 彼は通りを行ったり来たりした。

ex.en: He walked back and forth in the room.
ex.ja: 彼は部屋の中を行きつもどりつした。

note.ja: 古英語 forth（前へ）から。fore、further と同系。「前へ」→ back and forth（行ったり来たり）。

en: A short jump.
A jump on one leg.
To jump a short distance.
To jump on one foot.

hop.ety:
From Middle English hoppen, from Old English hoppian (“to hop, spring, leap, dance”), from Proto-West Germanic *huppōn, from Proto-Germanic *huppōną (“to hop”), from Proto-Indo-European *kewb- (“to bend, bow”).
Cognate with Dutch hoppen (“to hop”), German hopfen, hoppen (“to hop”), Danish hoppe (“to hop, leap, jump”), Swedish hoppa (“to hop, leap, jump”), Icelandic hoppa (“to hop, skip”).

ex.en: On Sunday, Tom went hop-picking on the farm.
ex.ja: 日曜日、トムは農場へホップを収穫にいってきました。

ex.en: Job hopping was not so common in Japan as in America.
ex.ja: 日本ではアメリカほど転職は一般的ではなかった。

ex.en: He hopped on a freight train bound for New York.
ex.ja: 彼はニューヨーク行きの貨物列車に飛び乗った。

note.ja: 古英語 hoppian から。「片足で跳ぶ」→ 店などを「はしごする（bar-hopping）」。

en: Exhibiting unsoundness or disorder of mind; not sane; utterly mad.
Used by or relating to insane people.

insane.ety: From Latin īnsānus (“unsound in mind; mad, insane”), from in- + sānus (“sound, sane”), equivalent to in- + sane.

ex.en: She was released on the grounds that she was insane.
ex.ja: 彼女は正気でないという理由で釈放された。

ex.en: That old man must be insane.
ex.ja: あの老人は頭がおかしいにちがいない。

ex.en: The man must be insane.
ex.ja: その男は頭がおかしいに違いない。

note.ja: in（否定）+ san（健康な）。健全でない →「正気でない・ばかげた」。sanitary（衛生的な）も同じ san。

en: To connect, set up or prepare something for use
To transfer software onto a device's permanent storage and put it in a state where it is ready to be run when needed, usually decompressi…
An installation: the process of installing a software application.
An installation: a software application that has been installed.

install.ety: From Middle English installen, from Old French installer, from Medieval Latin īnstallō (“to install, put in place, establish”), from in- + stallum (“stall”), from Frankish *stall (“stall, position, place”), from Proto-Germanic *stallaz (“place, position”), from Proto-Indo-European *stel-, *stAlǝn-, *stAlǝm- (“stem, trunk”). Cognate with Old High German stal (“location, stall”), Old English steall (“position, stall”), Old English onstellan (“to institute, create, originate, establish, give the example of”), Middle High German anstalt (“institute”), German anstellen (“to conduct, employ”), Germa

ex.en: They installed him as chairman of the committee.
ex.ja: 彼らは彼を委員会の議長に就任させた。

ex.en: I installed an operating system on my computer.
ex.ja: 自分のパソコンにOSをインストールしました。

ex.en: I want to have a telephone installed.
ex.ja: 電話を引きたいのです。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 installare ＝ in + stallum（席）。「席につかせる」→「就任させる」→「取り付ける」。stall と同じ。

en: A person from Israel or of Israeli descent.
Of, from, or pertaining to Israel or the Israeli people.

Israeli.ety:
From Hebrew ישראלי (jiśrəʾēlî). By surface analysis, Israel + -i.
Usage as a synonym for "Modern Israeli Hebrew" was popularized by Ghil'ad Zuckermann.

ex.en: The symbol used for the Israeli Shekel is "₪".
ex.ja: イスラエルシュケルを表す記号は「₪」です。

An extra scored when the batsmen take runs after the ball has passed the striker without hitting either the bat or the batsman.
Out of the way; remote.
Secondary; supplementary.
Goodbye.

bye.ety: Variant form of by, from Old English bī (“being near”).

ex.en: It is high time we said good-bye.
ex.ja: そろそろ別れを告げてもいいころだ。

ex.en: He left without saying good-bye to me.
ex.ja: 彼は私に別れを言わずに去った。

ex.en: How do you say "good bye" in German?
ex.ja: ドイツ語で「さようなら」をどう言いますか。

note.ja: goodbye の短縮。

en: To be in battle or in a rivalry with another for the same thing, position, or reward; to contend.
To be in a position in which it is possible to win or triumph.

compete.ety: Borrowed from Middle French competer, from Latin competere (“to coincide, to be equal to, to be capable of”), from com- (“with”) + petō (“to seek; to aim for, strive for”). Compare Latin competītor (“competitor”).

ex.en: Family members should not compete against each other.
ex.ja: 家族の中ではお互いに競争すべきではない。

ex.en: I had to compete with him for promotion.
ex.ja: 私は昇進をかけて彼と競争しなければならなかった。

ex.en: We must cut down on prices; we can't compete.
ex.ja: 価格を下げなければなりません。競争力がなくなってしまいます。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pet（求める）。一緒に同じものを求める →「競争する」。

en: A lineup or sequence of railroad carriages or cars, with or without a locomotive, that form a unit.

consist.ety: From Middle French consister, from Latin consistō (“stand together, stop, become hard or solid, agree with, continue, exist”), from com- (“together”) + sistō (“to cause to stand, stand”).

ex.en: This drama consists of just two short scenes.
ex.ja: この芝居は２つの短い場面で構成されている。

ex.en: The other committee consists of four members.
ex.ja: もう一つの委員会は４人のメンバーから出来ています。

ex.en: A basketball team consists of five players.
ex.ja: バスケットボールのチームは５人のメンバーで構成されている。

note.ja: con（共に）+ sist（立つ）。一緒に立っている →「〜から成る（of）・〜にある（in）」。

en: To give something that is or becomes part of a larger whole.

contribute.ety:
PIE word
 *tréyes
From Latin contribūtus, perfect passive participle of contribuō (“to bring together; to unite”), from con- (“together”) + tribuō (“to bestow”), from tribus (“tribe”), derived from trēs (“three”), from Proto-Italic *trēs, from Proto-Indo-European *tréyes.

ex.en: He contributed to the good of the community.
ex.ja: 彼は社会の福利のために貢献してくれた。

ex.en: He contributed a lot of money to the charity.
ex.ja: 彼はその慈善団体に多額の金を寄付した。

ex.en: He contributed a lot of money to the hospital.
ex.ja: 彼はその病院に多額の寄付をした。

note.ja: con（共に）+ trib（割り当てる）+ ute。一緒に分け与える →「貢献する・寄付する・寄稿する」。

en: An insect in the order Orthoptera, especially family Gryllidae, that makes a chirping sound by rubbing its wing casings against combs on …
A signalling device used by soldiers in hostile territory to identify themselves to a friendly in low visibility conditions.

cricket.ety:
From Middle English creket, crykett, crykette, from Old French criket (with diminutive -et) from criquer (“to make a cracking sound; creak”), from Middle Dutch kricken (“to creak; crack”), from Proto-West Germanic *krakōn, related to Middle English creken, criken (“to creak”), all ultimately of imitative origin.
Compare Dutch kriek (“cricket”), Middle Dutch krikel, criekel, crekel (“cricket”) (with diminituve -el), Middle Low German krikel, krekel (“cricket”), German Kreckel (“cricket”). More at creak.

ex.en: I should like to join the cricket club.
ex.ja: クリケットクラブに入りたい。

ex.en: Just as the Americans like baseball, the British like cricket.
ex.ja: アメリカ人が野球を好むように、イギリス人はクリケットを好む。

ex.en: Tom is an able cricket player.
ex.ja: トムは有能なクリケット選手だ。

note.ja: 「コオロギ」は古フランス語 criquer（キーキー鳴る）から擬音的な語。競技の「クリケット」は中世オランダ語 krick（杖）からとされ別語。

en: A person who appraises the works of others.
A specialist in judging works of art.

critic.ety: Borrowed from Middle French critique, from Latin criticus, from Ancient Greek κριτικός (kritikós, “of or for judging, able to discern”), from κρίνω (krínō, “to judge”).

ex.en: Critics thought little of the play.
ex.ja: 批評家たちはその劇をあまり高く評価しなかった。

ex.en: Regard all art critics as useless and dangerous.
ex.ja: あらゆる芸術評論家達は無能であり危険な存在である。

ex.en: The author of this article is a famous critic.
ex.ja: この記事の筆者は有名な批評家だ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kritikos（判断できる）から。判断する人 →「批評家・批判する人」。

en: An unexpected natural or man-made catastrophe of substantial extent causing significant physical damage or destruction, loss of life or s…
An unfortunate or unpleasant occurrence, especially one resulting from an accident or something going wrong.

disaster.ety: From Middle French desastre, from Italian disastro, from dis- + astro (“star”), from Latin astrum (“star”), from Ancient Greek ἄστρον (ástron, “star”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂stḗr.

ex.en: That terrorist was to blame for the disaster.
ex.ja: その惨事はあのテロリストのせいだ。

ex.en: They were calm in the face of disaster.
ex.ja: 彼らは災難に遭っても冷静であった。

ex.en: Such a disaster won't come again in my time.
ex.ja: あのような災害は一生の内に二度とやってこないだろう。

note.ja: dis（悪い）+ aster（星）。悪い星回り（占星術から）→「災害・大失敗」。

en: The action of entering, or going in.
The act of taking possession, as of property, or of office.
To delight and fill with wonder.
To put into a trance.

entrance.ety: From Middle French entrance (“entry”). Replaced native Middle English ingang (“entrance, admission”), from Old English ingang (“ingress, entry, entrance”).

ex.en: Some people were hanging around at the entrance.
ex.ja: 数人の人が入り口でぶらついていた。

ex.en: Please hand in the papers at the entrance.
ex.ja: 入り口で書類を提出して下さい。

ex.en: They caught up with him at the entrance.
ex.ja: 彼らは入口で彼に追いついた。

note.ja: enter（入る）+ -ance。「入ること・入口・入学」。動詞の entrance（エントランス：うっとりさせる）は trance（恍惚）からで別語。

en: In an equal manner; in equal shares or proportion; with equal and impartial justice; evenly.
In equal degree or extent; just as.

ex.en: The two groups share equally in the company.
ex.ja: 二つのグループが半々に同社を所有している。

ex.en: You have to share the cake equally.
ex.ja: 君たちはケーキを平等に分けなければならない。

ex.en: The company is equally owned by the two groups.
ex.ja: 同社は、二つのグループが半々ずつ所有している。

note.ja: equ（等しい）+ al + ly。等しく →「平等に・同様に」。

en: The condition of being fit, suitable or appropriate.
The cultivation of an attractive and/or healthy physique.

fitness.ety: From fit + -ness. First attested in the 16th century, with the physical sense from 1935.

ex.en: The physical fitness courses are required for everyone.
ex.ja: 体育の授業は全員が必修です。

ex.en: No one doubts her fitness for the post.
ex.ja: 彼女がその地位にふさわしいということは、だれも疑っていない。

ex.en: She exercises every day at a fitness club.
ex.ja: 彼女はフィットネスクラブで毎日訓練する。

note.ja: fit（適した・健康な）+ -ness。「適性」→「健康」。

en: The condition of being friends.
A friendly relationship, or a relationship as friends.

From Middle English frendschipe, frendshipe, from Old English frēondsċiepe, from Proto-West Germanic *friundskapi. Equivalent to friend + -ship.

ex.en: A true friendship is more valuable than money.
ex.ja: 真の友情はお金より尊い。

ex.en: I value your friendship more than anything.
ex.ja: 私は何より君の友情が大事だ。

ex.en: I am bound to him by a close friendship.
ex.ja: 私は固い友情で彼と結ばれている。

note.ja: friend + -ship。「友情」。

en: Idiotic, stupid.

idiot.ety:

From Middle English idiote, ydiote, from Old French idiote (later idiot), from Latin idiota, from Ancient Greek ἰδιώτης (idiṓtēs, “a private citizen, one who has no professional knowledge, layman”), from ἴδιος (ídios, “one's own, pertaining to oneself, private”). Doublet of idiota. By surface analysis, idi- + -ot.

ex.en: Where does that idiot think he is going?
ex.ja: あの馬鹿、どこへ行くつもりだ？

ex.en: Why do you love an idiot like me?
ex.ja: こんなばかな私をどうして愛してくれるの？

ex.en: I'm what the world calls an idiot.
ex.ja: 俺は世間で言うアホです。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 idiōtēs（私人・素人）から。idios（自分の）。公の事に関わらない人 →「無知な人」→「ばか」。idiom と同じ idio。

en: Of a characteristic: extreme or very high or strong in degree; severe; also, excessive, towering.
Of a thing: possessing some characteristic to an extreme or very high or strong degree.

intense.ety: From Late Middle English intens, intense (“ardent, fervent; extreme, great, intense”), borrowed from Old French intense (modern French intense), or directly from its etymon Latin intēnsus (“strained, stretched tight; intense; attentive; violent; (rare) eager, intent”), the perfect passive participle of intendō (“to stretch out, strain”), from in- (prefix meaning ‘in, inside, within’) + tendō (“to extend, stretch”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *tend- (“to extend, stretch”)).

ex.en: This intense heat doesn't seem to bother you.
ex.ja: こんなに暑いのに君は平気みたいだね。

ex.en: I had an intense pain in the head.
ex.ja: 頭に激しい痛みがあった。

ex.en: How are you keeping off this intense heat?
ex.ja: 猛暑をどうしのいでいますか。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ tens（伸ばす）+ e。ぴんと張りつめた →「激しい・強烈な」。

en: The duration of the life of someone or something.
A long period of time.

lifetime.ety: From Middle English lyftyme, equivalent to life + time. Cognate with Icelandic líftími (“lifetime”). Compare also Saterland Frisian Lieuwendstied, Dutch leeftijd and levenstijd, German Low German Levenstied, German Lebenszeit, Danish livstid, Swedish livstid.

ex.en: Her dream of a lifetime finally came true.
ex.ja: 彼女の一生の夢がついに叶った。

ex.en: This is the chance of a lifetime.
ex.ja: これは私の生涯にとって千載一遇の機会だ。

ex.en: Communism will never be reached in my lifetime.
ex.ja: 私の生きているうちに共産主義が効力を持つことは無いだろう。

note.ja: life（一生）+ time。「生涯」。

en: A substance that is flowing, and keeping no shape, such as water; a substance of which the molecules, while not tending to separate from …
Any of a class of consonant sounds that includes l and r.
Flowing freely like water; fluid; not solid and not gaseous; composed of particles that move freely among each other on the slightest pre…
Easily sold or disposed of without losing value.

From Middle English liquide, from Old French liquide, from Latin liquidus (“fluid, liquid, moist”), from liqueō (“to be liquid, be fluid”). Doublet of liquidus. As a term for a consonant, it comes from Latin liquida (cōnsōnāns), a calque of Ancient Greek

ex.en: You should not drink a lot of liquid.
ex.ja: 水分を控えてください。

ex.en: The liquid gave off a strong smell.
ex.ja: その液体は強烈な匂いを発した。

ex.en: You should drink a lot of liquid.
ex.ja: 水分をたくさん取ってください。

note.ja: ラテン語 liquidus（流れる）から。liquere（液体である）。「液体」→ 資産の「流動性」。

en: An item's composition.
Cosmetics; colorants and other substances applied to the skin to alter its appearance.

makeup.ety: Deverbal from make up. Noun sense 2 is a semantic loan from French maquillage, from maquiller (“to make up, fabricate”).

ex.en: My mother put on makeup before going out.
ex.ja: 母は出かける前に化粧をした。

ex.en: I don't like heavy makeup on a young girl.
ex.ja: 私は若い娘の厚化粧は好まない。

ex.en: She was a sight when she didn't wear makeup.
ex.ja: 彼女がお化粧してないときは見ものだった。

note.ja: make up（作り上げる・化粧する）の名詞化。「構成」と「化粧」。

en: A stamped metal disc used as a personal ornament, a charm, or a religious object.
A stamped or cast metal object (usually a disc), particularly one awarded as a prize or reward.
To win a medal.
To award a medal to.

medal.ety: From Middle English [Term?], from Middle French medaille, medale, from Italian medaglia (originally "half a denarius"), from Early Medieval Latin medālia, feminine derived via dissimilation (/dj–lj/ > /d–lj/) from mediālia, neuter plural of Late Latin mediālis (“middle”, adjective), from Classical Latin medius.

ex.en: He's been awarded a gold medal once.
ex.ja: 彼はいちど金メダルをもらったことがある。

ex.en: They awarded him a gold medal for his achievement.
ex.ja: 彼らは彼の業績に対して金メダルを授与した。

ex.en: It was the first gold medal that she had won.
ex.ja: それは彼女がとった最初の金メダルだった。

note.ja: イタリア語 medaglia（小さな硬貨）から。ラテン語 metallum（金属）。metal と同じ語源。

en: A legal agreement in which a borrower pledges real property as collateral for a loan used to purchase or refinance that property.
To borrow against a property, to obtain a loan for another purpose by giving away the right of seizure to the lender over a fixed propert…
To pledge and make liable; to make subject to obligation; to achieve an immediate result by paying for it in the long term.

mortgage.ety: From Middle English morgage and Middle French mortgage, from Anglo-Norman morgage, from Old French mort gage (“dead pledge”), after a translation of judicial Medieval Latin mortuum wadium, with wadium from Frankish *wadi (“wager, pledge”). Compare gage and also wage. So called because rents and profits from the land were owed to the lender for as long as the gage existed (comparable to interest on a loan today), as opposed to the living gage, in which rents and profits automatically reduced the debt (paying it off over time).

ex.en: The bank holds a mortgage on his building.
ex.ja: 銀行は彼のビルを抵当に取っている。

ex.en: My house is a mortgage-free house.
ex.ja: 私の家はローンの支払いが終わいる。

ex.en: I suffered from my mortgage loan.
ex.ja: 私は住宅ローンで苦しんだ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 mort（死んだ）+ gage（担保）。返済すれば「死ぬ（消える）」担保 →「抵当・住宅ローン」。mortal と同じ mort。

en: Telling a story.
Overly talkative; garrulous.
The systematic recitation of an event or series of events.
That which is narrated.

narrative.ety: Borrowed from Middle Scots narrative, nerrative, from Middle French narratif, from Latin narrātīvus, from narrō (“to narrate”). By surface analysis, Latin narr- + -ate + -ive.

ex.en: That is not what the narrative is about.
ex.ja: それはその物語の述べるところではない。

ex.en: She gave a narrative of her strange experience.
ex.ja: 彼女は自分の奇妙な経験を語った。

ex.en: The mystery contains more dialogue than narrative.
ex.ja: その推理小説は地の文よりも会話の部分の方が多い。

note.ja: ラテン語 narrare（語る）から。「物語・語り」。narrator、narrate と同じ。

en: Having a small width; not wide; having opposite edges or sides that are close, especially by comparison to length or depth.
Of little extent; very limited; circumscribed.
A narrow passage, especially a contracted part of a stream, lake, or sea; a strait connecting two bodies of water.
To reduce in width or extent; to contract.
To get narrower.

narrow.ety:
From Middle English narow, narowe, narewe, narwe, naru, from Old English nearu (“narrow, strait, confined, constricted, not spacious, limited, petty; limited, poor, restricted; oppressive, causing anxiety (of that which restricts free action of body or mind), causing or accompanied by difficulty, hardship, oppressive; oppressed, not having free action; strict, severe”), from Proto-West Germanic *naru, from Proto-Germanic *narwaz (“constricted, narrow”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ner- (“to turn, bend, twist, constrict”).
Cognates
Cognate with North Frisian naar, noar, noor, nåår (“narrow”),

ex.en: The gate is too narrow for a car.
ex.ja: その門は狭すぎて車は入れません。

ex.en: The gate was too narrow for the truck.
ex.ja: 門はトラックには狭過ぎた。

ex.en: This house is too narrow to live in.
ex.ja: この家は住むには狭すぎる。

note.ja: 古英語 nearu から。「狭い」→「きわどい」（a narrow escape）。

en: To notice or view, especially carefully or with attention to detail.
To follow or obey the custom, practice, or rules (especially of a religion).

observe.ety: From Middle French observer, from Old French observer, from Latin observō (“to watch”), from ob- (“before”) + servō (“to keep”), from Proto-Indo-European *ser- (“to guard”). Cognate with Gothic 𐍃𐌰𐍂𐍅𐌰 (sarwa, “weapons, armour”), Old English searu (“device”).

ex.en: The boy observed the growth of the plant.
ex.ja: その少年は植物の成長を観察した。

ex.en: I observed that it had already got dark.
ex.ja: あたりがもう暗くなっていることに気がついた。

ex.en: The police observed the man enter the bank.
ex.ja: 警察はその男が銀行に入るのを見つけた。

note.ja: ob（〜に向かって）+ serv（保つ・見守る）。注意深く見守る →「観察する・（規則を）守る・述べる」。

en: On occasion: at relatively infrequent intervals, from time to time, sometimes.

occasionally.ety: From Middle English occasionally, occasionaly, occasyoneely, occasyonly, equivalent to occasional + -ly.

ex.en: Let's occasionally change where we go to eat out.
ex.ja: いつもと変えてたまに外で食事しよう。

ex.en: The speaker occasionally referred to his notes.
ex.ja: 講演者は時折メモを参照した。

ex.en: I occasionally meet him at the club.
ex.ja: 時折クラブで彼に会います。

note.ja: occasional（時折の）+ -ly。ラテン語 occasio（好機）、ob + cadere（落ちる）。「降ってきた機会に」→「ときどき」。

en: A wide, flat receptacle used around the house, especially for cooking.
The contents of such a receptacle.
To wash in a pan (of earth, sand etc. when searching for gold).
To disparage; to belittle; to put down; to harshly criticize, especially a work (book, movie, etc.)
Pansexual or panromantic.

ex.en: Don't touch that pan! It's very hot.
ex.ja: その鍋に触らないで。すごく熱いから。

ex.en: The handle of this pan is easy to hold.

ex.en: Did you put oil in the pan?
ex.ja: 鍋に油入れた？

en: The branch of science concerned with the study of the properties and interactions of space, time, matter and energy.
The physical aspects of a phenomenon or a system, especially those examined or studied scientifically.

physics.ety: 1580s; from physic (see also -ics), from Middle English phisik, from Old French fisike (“natural science, art of healing”), from Latin physica (“study of nature”), from Ancient Greek φυσική (phusikḗ), feminine singular of φυσικός (phusikós, “natural; physical”), from Ancient Greek φύσις (phúsis, “origin; nature, property”), from Ancient Greek φύω (phúō, “produce; bear; grow”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH- (“to appear, become, rise up”).

ex.en: Some students like English, and others like physics.
ex.ja: 英語の好きな生徒もいるし、物理の好きな生徒もいる。

ex.en: I have to bone up on my physics.
ex.ja: 私は一生懸命物理に取り組まなければならない。

ex.en: I'm not in the least interested in physics.
ex.ja: 私は物理に少しも興味がない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 physika（自然のこと）から。physis（自然）。「物理学」。physical、physician と同じ。

en: The act, process, or result of reducing.
The amount or rate by which something is reduced, e.g. in price.

reduction.ety: From Middle English reduccion, a borrowing from Old French reducion, from Latin reductiō, reductiōnem. Equivalent to reduce + -tion.

ex.en: A further reduction would make us go into the red.
ex.ja: これ以上の値引きは、私どもを赤字に追いやるでしょう。

ex.en: We would ask you to give us a price reduction of 5%.
ex.ja: それを５％値引きしていただけますか。

ex.en: We cannot offer a further price reduction under the current circumstances.
ex.ja: 現状では、これ以上の値引きはいたしかねます。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ duct（導く）+ ion。元へ引き戻すこと →「削減・縮小」。reduce（減らす）。

en: To bend back (light, etc.) from a surface.
To be bent back (light, etc.) from a surface.

reflect.ety: From Old French reflecter (“to bend back, turn back”), from Latin reflectō (“to reflect”), from re- (“again”) + flectō (“to bend, to curve”). Compare English reflex.

ex.en: This decision will reflect on his future career.
ex.ja: この決定は彼の将来に悪影響をもたらすだろう。

ex.en: It is time to reflect on your past.
ex.ja: 自分の過去をじっくり振り返ってみてもよいころだ。

ex.en: It's time to reflect on your past.
ex.ja: 自分の過去をじっくり振り返ってみてもよいころだ。

note.ja: re（後ろへ）+ flect（曲げる）。光を後ろへ曲げ返す →「反射する・反映する・よく考える」。

en: Laughable or amusing through foolishness or a foolish appearance.
Absurdly large.
Sillily: in a silly manner.
A silly person.
A term of address.

silly.ety:
From Middle English seely, sēlī, from Old English sǣliġ, ġesǣliġ (“lucky, fortunate”), from Proto-West Germanic *sālīg, from *sāli; equivalent to seel (“happiness, bliss”) + -y. Doublet of Seelie.
The semantic evolution is “lucky” to “innocent” to “naive” to “foolish”. Compare the similar evolution of daft (originally meaning “accommodating”), and almost the reverse with nice (originally meaning “ignorant”).

ex.en: I need to ask you a silly question.
ex.ja: バカな質問があるんだ。

ex.en: It was silly of you to trust them.
ex.ja: 君がやつらを信じたのはばかだった。

ex.en: How can you say such a silly thing?
ex.ja: どうしてそんな馬鹿な事が言えるんですか。

note.ja: 古英語 sǣlig（幸せな・祝福された）から。「無邪気な」→「ばかな」に意味が変わった。

en: Following in time; coming or being after something else at any time, indefinitely.
Following in order of place; succeeding.
A subsequent stream or faultline.

subsequent.ety:

ex.en: I want quick action subsequent to the decision.
ex.ja: 決定の後すみやかに実行に移して欲しい。

ex.en: Knowledge has been passed down to subsequent generation.
ex.ja: 知識はその次の世代へと次々に伝えられてきた。

note.ja: ラテン語 subsequi ＝ sub（すぐ後に）+ sequi（続く）。「その後の」。sequence と同じ sequ。

en: The conversion of text from one language to another.
The discipline or study of translating written language (as opposed to interpretation, which concerns itself with spoken language).

translation.ety: From Middle English translacioun (“transfer, translation”), from Anglo-Norman translacioun, from Latin trānslātiō, from trānslāt-, the supine stem of trānsferō (“to transfer, transport, transform, translate”). Equivalent to translate + -ion. Displaced native Old English wending.

ex.en: Set your translation against the original once again.
ex.ja: もう一度翻訳を原文と比較してみなさい。

ex.en: The translation is quite true to the original.
ex.ja: その翻訳は原文に極めて忠実である。

ex.en: In this case, translation is, in effect, impossible.
ex.ja: この場合は、翻訳は事実上不可能だ。

note.ja: translate（翻訳する）+ -ion。trans（向こうへ）+ latus（運ばれた）。「言葉を向こう側へ運ぶこと」。

en: Able to be seen.

visible.ety: From Middle English visible, from Old French visible, from Late Latin visibilis (“that may be seen”), from Latin videre (“to see”), past participle visus; see vision. Displaced native Old English ġesewenlīċ.

amendment.ety: From French amendement, from Late Latin amendamentum, equivalent to amend + -ment.

ex.en: The committee proposed an amendment to the law.
